objective: Establish one typed budget-period read contract for scope, forecast, history, and PostgreSQL grouping while correcting weekly bucket parity without changing public API, schema, or writers.

read_contract: daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and yearly are parsed strictly once at read boundaries
containing range, period shifting, and bucket keys share one typed core owner
weekly uses Monday as the first day and POSIX percent-W week 00 before the first Monday
PostgreSQL forecast grouping matches Rust bucket keys across day, week, month, quarter, and year boundaries
explicit unknown forecast and history periods fail before any database query
unchanged_boundaries: REST paths, request and response DTOs, default monthly behavior, and frontend code
PostgreSQL user scope, schema, migrations, and transaction ownership
budget hierarchy writers and their existing string-based period synchronization
integer-cent money fields, forecast payload shape, and category filtering
rejected_expansion: new service, trait, UnitOfWork, crate, cache, compatibility adapter, or second writer
database CHECK constraint or writer cutover before a separately approved migration slice
formal bill draft and export renderer abstractions unrelated to the period identity drift

weekly_drift_before_fix: 2021-01-01: PostgreSQL YYYY-WW produced 2021-01 while Rust percent-W produced 2021-00
2021-01-10: PostgreSQL YYYY-WW produced 2021-02 while Rust percent-W produced 2021-01
2026-05-07: PostgreSQL YYYY-WW produced 2026-19 while Rust percent-W produced 2026-18

red.result: failed because the public weekly forecast returned current_spent_cents 0 instead of 1200 under PostgreSQL YYYY-WW
failed to compile before BudgetPeriodKind existed
failed to compile before the typed range and bucket operations existed
failed before public forecast and history entrypoints parsed periods strictly

cargo_test_workspace.result: passed against a fresh temporary PostgreSQL gate database

cargo_llvm_cov_workspace.result: passed with CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 against a fresh temporary PostgreSQL gate database

changed_line_coverage.method: scripts/governance-normalizers.mjs summarizeChangedLineCoverage over the base-to-working-tree Rust diff supplied on stdin

review.standards_axis: passed with no findings: period behavior is a small concrete core value object; PostgreSQL remains a concrete adapter; no trait, service, transaction owner, schema, cache, or writer was added
review.spec_axis: passed with no findings: scope, forecast, on-demand history, and SQL grouping share typed period semantics; weekly percent-W parity and unknown-period fail-closed behavior are proven on real PostgreSQL
review.test_gap: Three changed executable pass-through lines in the on-demand history adapter were not directly hit; the underlying history range semantics and public unknown-period entrypoint are covered, and aggregate changed-line coverage is 97.56 percent.
review.residual_risk: The hierarchy writer still interprets raw period strings and the database has no period_type CHECK constraint; both are deliberately retained for a separate data-aware writer migration slice.

verification.money_review: No money field or conversion changed; budget and forecast values remain integer cents.
verification.delivery_evidence: The Gitea PR and exact-head Actions record remain the authoritative external delivery evidence, so their immutable run identifiers are not written into the head they verify.

environment_hygiene.test_database_strategy: full workspace tests and coverage each used a dedicated temporary PostgreSQL database and removed it with FORCE after completion
environment_hygiene.long_lived_development_database: audited read-only for period values and constraints; not migrated, cleared, or used as a mutable test fixture
environment_hygiene.secrets: PostgreSQL credentials were read from the existing local container only inside process scope and were not printed or persisted
